translations.answer: In the three-degree-of-freedom waist Unitree G1 simulation setup of ULC, skills are opened in the order of speed, height, torso/arms, combined with forward feed of arm actions with residuals, command interpolation/delay, payload randomization, and CoM reward, allowing training of a single policy that covers a large command space; evidence does not support extrapolation to complex leg actions or uncontrolled contact tasks.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Target tasks can be commanded by root velocity/height, torso orientation and arm joint positions.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: A 3-DoF-waist Unitree G1-like embodiment and procedural command sampler are available.
translations.confidence_rationale: Large simulation comparisons and component ablations support the design, but baseline interfaces differ, public code is unavailable, and real task evidence is mainly qualitative.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figure 2, Equations 25-26, Tables III-V and Figure 5
translations.evidence.0.note: Supports unified command tracking, residual arm action and component ablations.
